body:
Add a pure-Rust URDF machine-model loader and 6-DOF link poser in `camcraft-sim::machine_model`.

## Context
Research in #2593 designed the URDF file contract for machine models (including SolidCraft URDF exports, which write binary STL meshes in meters). `camcraft-sim` reads only plain data and files; it keeps zero dependency on `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-app`, or SolidCraft at run time.

## Scope
- Extend `crates/sim/src/machine_model/` (`check.rs`, `pose.rs`, `shape.rs`, `mod.rs`):
  - Extend link transforms in `pose.rs` from translation-only `offset` to a 6-DOF rigid frame (`offset` + fixed-axis XYZ `rpy`) so URDF `<origin xyz="..." rpy="..."/>` and `root_frame` compose accurately. Existing `MachineSpec` callers keep identity rotation.
  - Add `BodySource::Urdf` (not marked "generated"; `judged_on()` distinguishes it from `BodySource::Generated`).
  - Add closed sphere tessellation (`shape::sphere`) alongside `shape::block` and `shape::cylinder` for URDF inline primitives.
- Add a pure-Rust W3C XML 1.0 URDF reader in `crates/sim/src/machine_model/` (zero new external crate dependencies; follow `crates/tools/src/tool_table_xml.rs`, keeping attributes, nesting limit 32, and refusing `<!DOCTYPE` / `<!ENTITY`).
- Accept plain-data mapping input (`UrdfLoadSpec`: base directory, URDF XML or path, axis-to-joint map with `sign`, `zero`, axis kind, optional `.mch` travel, optional `root_frame`, optional `tool_link` and `table_link`).
- Convert URDF SI units at load: multiply lengths (`<origin xyz>`, primitives, prismatic `<limit>`, and mesh vertices after `<mesh scale>`) by `1000.0` (`m -> mm`), and convert angles (`<origin rpy>`, revolute `<limit>`) from radians to degrees.
- Load `<collision>` geometry first for each link; if `<collision>` is absent, fall back to `<visual>` with a named note; if neither exists, emit no body and a named note.
- Support `<box>`, `<cylinder>`, `<sphere>`, and `<mesh filename scale>` for `.stl` and `.obj` via `camcraft-geometry`. Validate closed 2-manifold topology for collision meshes (matching `FixtureMesh::build`).
- Keep `.mch` travel authoritative for program limits: record a named discrepancy note in `MachineModel::notes` when URDF `<limit>` disagrees with `.mch` travel, and expose URDF mechanical joint bounds so `pose` or a mechanical-limit helper reports out-of-range joints without silent clamping.
- Enforce every named refusal from #2593:
  - Unmapped moving joint (`revolute`, `continuous`, `prismatic`), mapped `fixed` joint, or unsupported joint type (`floating`, `planar`, unknown).
  - Driven axis letter with no joint, unknown joint name, duplicate letter or joint mapping, or linear/rotary kind mismatch.
  - Closed kinematic chain (cycle or link with two parent joints), self-parent joint, zero or multiple root links, unknown link reference, or duplicate link/joint names.
  - Missing mesh file, absolute path, remote or `package://` URI, unsupported extension (`.glb`, `.gltf`, `.dae`), corrupt STL/OBJ, mesh over `MAX_MESH_TRIS`, or open/non-manifold collision mesh.
  - Non-finite values, zero `<axis>`, reversed `<limit>`, non-positive primitive sizes or `<mesh scale>`, more than `MAX_PARTS` links, or malformed/unsafe XML.

## Done means
Tests in `crates/sim/tests/` pin: (1) loading and posing a 3-axis and a 5-axis URDF fixture (inline primitives, binary and ASCII STL, OBJ, `<mesh scale>`, and `<collision>` preference over `<visual>`), (2) `m -> mm` and `rad -> deg` conversion with `root_frame`, `sign`, and `zero`, (3) `BodySource::Urdf` provenance, (4) `.mch`-wins limit discrepancy notes and mechanical limit reporting, and (5) every named refusal above.

Depends on #3639.

Part of #2593
